questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent fatigue on a long ride?

options.text: Limit how far you ride in one day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue, dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants. When they wear off, you may feel extreme fatigue.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, shift down and ride slowly toward it. Then accelerate and leave the dog behind.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You rarely hear a tire going flat on a motorcycle. Tire failure usually shows up as a change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: Other drivers have trouble seeing motorcycles at night. What should a motorcycle rider do?

options.text: Reduce your speed when riding at night.
Honk your horn repeatedly when riding at night.
Ride directly in front of another vehicle so their headlights light you up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when riding at night.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of the car ahead to help you see farther. Use your high beam unless you are following or meeting another vehicle. Be ready to change your lane position.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which instruction should you NOT give them?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as you can without crowding me.
Hold firmly onto my waist, hips, or belt.
Feel free to talk whenever you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel free to talk whenever you want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet and avoid moving. They should only get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: How does the stopping distance for motorcycles compare to cars?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Both take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. However, wet or slippery roads make it much harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, all of the following matter, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks nice.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all around with no visible damage such as cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What should you do when going through a curve?

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Always stay on the left side of the lane.
Always stay on the right side of the lane.
Remember that the best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remember that the best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change at any time. Be ready to change your lane position. The safest path through a curve may not match the road's actual curve.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, flash your brake light before slowing down. The tailgater may be focused on you and not see hazards that require traffic to slow down.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle windshields?

options.text: They work as well as a face shield.
They work as well as goggles.
They do not protect your eyes from wind.
They protect against items thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good replacement for a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: If road conditions require a longer stopping distance than normal, what should you do?

options.text: Follow the car ahead more closely.
Stay farther behind the car ahead.
Let someone else ride your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car ahead.
questions.explanation: You need more space between your motorcycle and the car ahead if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. In wet conditions, when you cannot see past the car ahead, or in heavy traffic, use at least a three-second following distance.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) makes a person age 21 or older legally intoxicated?
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and unsafe to ride a motorcycle while drunk.

questions.question: When should a passenger get on a motorcycle?

options.text: As far back on the seat as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: After the engine starts.
questions.explanation: A passenger should only get on a motorcycle after the engine is started and the transmission is in neutral. The passenger should sit as far forward as possible without interfering with the operator's control and should hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle operator position themselves in a traffic lane?

options.text: Always in the same part of the lane.
Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always in the center of the lane.
Always on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best or should always be avoided. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly and slowly increase front brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load on your motorcycle, what should you adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: The suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the recommended settings for the added weight.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds under 30 mph.

questions.question: There is usually an oily strip in the middle of the lane. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid it when the road is wet.
Ride on it because it provides better traction.
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane.
Do not worry about oil or other items in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks builds up in the center of each lane. On dry roads, this strip usually has enough traction for a motorcycle. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or put them in saddlebags. Placing loads high on a sissy bar or frame raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and affects balance. Always spread loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: What do studies show about riders in crashes?

options.text: They don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
They brake the front tire too much and don't brake the rear tire enough.
They only use the front brake.
They only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: They don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders involved in crashes don't use the front brake enough and use the rear brake too much.

questions.question: What is the best way to ride a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve exactly. You might need to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. Is this area safe for motorcycles?

options.text: Usually safe, except when the road is wet.
Usually safe, except when it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, except when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles to ride safely. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side of it and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar when a motorcycle accelerates?

options.text: It feels like it is falling behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to the motorcycle. Because of its weight and inertia, it will feel like it is falling behind when you accelerate.
